1. More people were interested in visiting Paris than New York, and more people were interested in visiting New York than Tokyo
2. The number of people interested in visiting at most two destinations is three times that of those interested in visiting exactly three.
3. Exactly 50 people were interested in visiting exactly one destination. 
4. The number of people interested in visiting exactly two destinations is at least 20.

Using the given information, answer the following questions.
questions.question_text:
Additional information: The CEO of MakeMyTrip asked the surveying team to resurvey and add "Rome" as another destination to be surveyed among the 160 premium members. The team conducted the survey again and realised that even after including Rome, all of the previous conditions mentioned in the instructions still held, and more people were interested in visiting Rome than Tokyo and less than New York. During the second survey, some members changed their destinations of interest.

The number of people interested in visiting at least one destination is the maximum possible and the number of people interested in visiting all four destinations is the minimum possible. If the difference between the number of people interested in visiting Tokyo and visiting Paris is as low as possible, what is the total number of people interested in visiting Rome?
questions.solution_text:
We are told that all previous conditions still stand even after including Rome; now, we are optimising four destinations. 
Redrawing the equations, we have the following, 
$A$=Number of people interested in visiting exactly one destination
$B$=Number of people interested in visiting exactly two destinations
$C$=Number of people interested in visiting exactly three destinations
$D$=Number of people interested in visiting exactly four destinations
$E$=Number of people interested in visiting exactly zero destinations
We have the condition: The number of people interested in visiting at most two destinations is three times that of those interested in visiting exactly three. Now, since this condition stands, we have the equation, 
$E+A+B=3C$
Substituting this in the overall equation, $E+A+B+C+D=160$
$4C+D=160$
We are told that E and D equals 0. 
We have C=40, B=70, A=50
We want to distribute this so that there is a minimum difference between members interested in visiting Tokyo and Paris
Let us start by distributing C, the number of people interested in visiting three destinations. 
To make sure the difference is the minimum possible, let us start with the most equitable distribution. 
We have 40 people who were interested in visiting exactly three destinations, and we have four destinations to distribute to, this gives us 4 different combinations of destinations, being, 
Paris-New York-Rome
Paris-New York-Tokyo
New York-Rome-Tokyo
Paris-Rome-Tokyo
If 10 people were interested in visiting each of these combinations, that means 30 people went to each destination. 
Now coming to members interested in visiting exactly two destinations, we have six possible combinations of pairs of two from four destinations and 70 people to distribute; let us distribute them such that each destination has an equal number of people interested in visiting; we get that with this distribution of people. 
Paris-New York: 12
Paris-Rome: 11
Paris-Tokyo: 12
New York-Rome: 12
New York-Tokyo: 11
Rome-Tokyo: 12
We see that 35 people are interested in visiting each combination. 
Fifty people are left to be distributed that are interested in visiting exactly one destination. Now, we want to maintain the condition that, 
Paris>New York>Rome>Tokyo
We can divide 50 in the following manner: 11+12+13+14=50. 
The following distribution shows that the difference between members interested in visiting Tokyo and Paris is the minimum possible. 
The number of people who are interested in visiting Rome is 77.

questions.question_text: What is the value of $X^2$?
questions.solution_text:
We are given the following,
We are told that each square will be filled with a distinct digit from 1 to 9. The smallest number that can be formed as a sum of four single-digit numbers will be 10, 1+2+3+4.
When X is greater than 7, 2X will be greater than X+7. Since X has to be at least 10, this will be true.
Similarly, 3X-5 will be greater than 2X when X is greater than 5, which is true.
Hence, we can arrange the four numbers given in increasing order as X, X+7, 2X, 3X-5.
Now, we are told that the smallest of the four numbers, X, is a prime number.
We know the minimum sum of four single-digit numbers must be at least 10. So $X\ge10$
We also know that the maximum possible sum of four single-digit numbers is 30, which is 9+8+7+6.
So, $3X-5\le30$.
We get the following relations, $10\le X\le\frac{35}{3}$
The only prime number to fall in that range will be 11. Hence, X is equal to 11.

Tate Modern in London was setting up an exhibition of EIGHT Salvador Dali paintings, all framed in square shapes with distinct integer sides. The museum curator in charge decided to arrange these paintings together to fit them in a large rectangular frame, as shown below. After trying to fit the eight paintings in the large frame to the best of his abilities, he realised this arrangement left a gap. The paintings were arranged so that there was no gap between two sides of a painting. Upon measurement, it was found that the gap was also in the shape of an exact square of 1 foot on the side. 

Using the given information, find the remaining paintings' sizes and answer the questions.
questions.question_text: What is the area (in square feet) of the rectangle formed due to the arrangement?
questions.solution_text:
Let us observe the given figure, 
Let us assume painting A is on the side $x$. We are told that all paintings are squares, including the gap formed during the arrangement. 
The figure shows that the size of side painting B is equal to the sum of the side of painting A plus the side of the gap formed. Since we know the size of the gap formed, we can write the size of side B as $x+1$ since the size of the side is 1 foot. 
Similarly, the side of Painting C can be observed as the difference between the side of Painting A and the gap formed. Hence, we can write the size of Side C as $x-1$. 
Progressively, the side of Painting D can be observed as the difference between the side of Painting C and the gap formed. Hence, we can write the size of Side D as $x-2$. 
Now that we know the sizes of the sides of Painting C and D, we can write the side of Painting G as $(x-2)+(x-1)$, which equals $2x-3$. 
From the figure, we can observe that the side of Painting E + the side of Painting D equals the Side of Painting B plus the side of the gap formed. 
Drawing up the equation for that we get, $\left(x+1\right)+\left(1\right)=\left(x-2\right)$+Side of Painting E
We get the value of Side of Painting E as 4. 
Now that we know the size of the side of Painting E, we can write the Size of the side of Painting F as the Size of the side of Painting B plus the size of the side of Painting E, Giving us the size of the side of Painting F as $x+5$. 
Finally, we can try finding out the size of Side H. From Painting A, B and F; we see that the sum of the width of the rectangle is $x+(x+1)+(x+5)=(3x+6)$. From this expression, subtracting the side of Painting G, we have $(3x+6)-(2x-3)$, which equals $(x+9)$
Doing the same operation on the other side, we take the sum of sides A, C, and G. This gives us $(4x-4)$. If we subtract the side of F, we have $(3x-9)$. 
Since it is a square, we can equate either side to find the value of x, which we get as $(x+9)=(3x-9)$. Thus, we get the value of $x$ as 9. 
Using this, we have the following following sides of the paintings. 
A=9 feet
B=10 feet
C=8 feet
D=7 feet
E=4 feet
F=14 feet
G=15 feet
H=18 feet

The scores of the players against the other teams are given in the table below, with some missing values. Fill out the table using the clues given below.

1) Head and Abhi scored the same number of runs against Delhi, and similarly, Ishan and Rutu scored the same number of runs against Delhi.

2) The runs scored by Devon against Delhi and Rahul against Chennai are in 2 : 3 ratio.

3) Delhi scored the same number of runs in both of their games.

4) The runs scored by Rachin against Hyderabad, Rutu against Hyderabad, Stubbs against Chennai, Stubbs against Hyderabad and Ishan against Delhi are in increasing AP in that order.

5) Delhi beat Chennai by 6 runs, and the runs scored by Ishan against Chennai, Abhi against Delhi, and Abhi against Chennai are in a 1: 4: 6 ratio.

6) Hyderabad beat Chennai by 13 runs, and Hyderabad scored 193 runs against Delhi.

Answer the following questions based on the information given above.
questions.question_text: How many runs did Chennai score against Hyderabad?
questions.solution_text:
From (5), we can assume the scores of Ishan against Chennai, Abhi against Delhi, and Abhi against Chennai to be c, 4c and 6c.
In (4), let the score of Rachin against Hyderabad be x, and the common difference be d. The scores become x, x + d, x + 2d, x + 3d and x + 4d in the same order as given in the question.
From (1), the score of Head against Delhi becomes 4c as Ishan scored the same number of runs.
From (2), let the score of Devon against Delhi be 2a and Rahul against Chennai be 3a.
Filling all the assumptions in the table, it looks like,
From (3), we can write
87 + 61 + x + 3d = 3a + 53 + x + 2d
95 + d = 3a   ---(1)
From (5), as Delhi beat Chennai by 6 runs, we can write
x + 2d + 53 + 3a = 67 + x + 4d + 2a + 6
a = 2d + 20   ---(2)
3 * (2) and substituting it in (1), we get,
95 + d = 6d + 60
d = 7
a = 34
From (6), as Hyderabad beat Chennai by 13 runs, we get,
15 + 7c = x + x + d + 79 + 13
7c = 2x + 84   ----(3)
From (6), as Hyderabad scored 193 runs against Delhi, we get,
4c + 4c + x + 4d = 193
8c + x = 193 - 28
x = 165 - 8c  ----(4)
Substituting (4) in (3), we get,
7c = 2*(165 - 8c) + 84
7c = 330 - 16c + 84
23c = 414
c = 18 and x = 21

p + n + d + n + d + 5 + m + n = 250

p + m + n + d = 160 …(4)

(m + $3\cdot\frac{\left(n+d\right)}{2}$​ + p ) - ($3\cdot\frac{\left(n+d\right)}{2}$+p) = 200 -180 
m = 20

questions.question_text: On a particular day, Ramlal starts his deliveries from city A and has to make deliveries to each city. What is the minimum distance he must travel to visit each city exactly once and return to city A without using the same road twice?
questions.solution_text:
Starting from city A, eight routes can be taken to visit each city exactly once and return to city A.
If the first city visited after A is B, then the following four routes are possible:
1. A-B-F-G-D-E-C-A --> total distance = 6 + 7 + 11 + 12 + 6 + 4 + 8 = 54km
2. A-B-F-G-E-D-C-A --> total distance = 6 + 7 + 11 + 8 + 6 + 3 + 8 = 49km
3. A-B-F-E-G-D-C-A --> total distance = 6 + 7 + 5 + 8 + 12 + 3 + 8 = 49km
4. A-B-E-F-G-D-C-A --> total distance = 6 + 9 + 5 + 11 + 12 + 3 + 8 = 54km
If the first city visited after A is C, then all the above routes in the reverse order are possible:
1. A-C-D-G-F-E-B-A --> total distance = 54km
2. A-C-D-G-E-F-B-A --> total distance = 49km
3. A-C-D-E-G-F-B-A --> total distance = 49km
4. A-C-E-D-G-F-B-A --> total distance = 54km
Thus, we can observe that the minimum distance that must be travelled to visit each city once is 49km.
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

Each employee’s performance is rated on a scale of 1 to 10 for each metric. The  chart below shows the ratings of three employees (A, B, and C) across these metrics. 

Each metric is assigned a weight that reflects its importance in the overall performance evaluation. The weights for Quality of Work, Punctuality, Communication Skills are 0.6 and for the other three parameters, it is 0.4. The weighted score for any person is the weighted average of the individual ratings.

For example, if Quality of Work is rated 8, its contribution to the weighted score would be 8 × 0.6 = 4.8. The sum of the individual contributions would be the total weighted score. This total weighted score divided by the sum of weights would give the weighted average score.

A bonus (in Rs.) is given to each employee based on the weighted score i.e. Bonus = Weighted Average Score × 1000
questions.question_text: What is the highest weighted average rating among the three employees?

We can make the following table mentioning the ratings received by all three employees in each parameters. 
Weighted average rating for A = $\dfrac{\left(\left(10+6+5\right)\times0.6+\left(9+8+7\right)\times0.4\right)}{3\times0.6+3\times0.4}=7.4$
Weighted average rating for B = $\dfrac{\left(\left(6+8+10\right)\times0.6+\left(7+6+8\right)\times0.4\right)}{3\times0.6+3\times0.4}=7.6$
Weighted average rating for C = $\dfrac{\left(\left(9+7+8\right)\times0.6+\left(6+8+10\right)\times0.4\right)}{3\times0.6+3\times0.4}=8$
With this, we can say, the highest rating received by anyone is 8.

A person named “ROBEN” is a believer in Numerology.

He number-coded each letter of the alphabet as: A-1, B-2, C-3, … Z-26.

His wife's name has some numeric properties:

1) It is a five lettered word with no letters repeated.

2) Only the alphabet ‘N’ is common between his and his wife’s names.

3) The product of the number codes of the letters of both their names is the same.

4) The name does not have the alphabet ‘A’

5) The fourth letter from the left is the second smallest and if it is removed from the word, all the remaining letters are in alphabetical order.
questions.question_text: What is the number code for the first letter of his wife’s name?
questions.solution_text:
The product of letters of the husband ROBEN is 18*15*2*5*14 = $2^3*3^3*5^2*7$.
The same should be the product of letters of the wife’s name. 
We know that the alphabet ‘N’ is common.
So we have the value 14 now.
We need to get $3^3$ from the wife’s name. 
27 as an alphabet is not possible. 
We should either have three multiples of 3 or one multiple of 9 and one multiple of 3. 
Let’s assume there are three multiples of 3.
They can be from 3, 6, 12, 15, 18, 21and 24.
But 15 and 18 are letters in the husband’s name and they can be eliminated.
21 has an extra 7 and can be eliminated. 
We already have the alphabet with code 14 and if we have the alphabet with code 24 there will be $2^4$ which should not be.
So we are left with only 3, 6 and 12.
If all three of 3, 6 and 12 are present then we will again have $2^4$ which should not be there.
So in the wife’s name there must be two letters one a multiple of 9 and another a multiple of 3.
As 18 is already there in the husband’s name the wife’s name must have 9.
Now 14 and 9 are there and we must find the other 3 letters whose product must be $2^2*3*5^2$
There must be two 5s in her name. They can be in the form of two multiples of 5 or as 25.
If they are as two multiples of 5 they can be from among 5, 10, 15 and 20.
But 5 and 15 are already present in the husband’s name.
So only 10 and 20 are possible.
If 10 and 20 both cannot be present as then we will have $2^4$ in the wife’s name which should not be.
So 25 must be present in the wife’s name.
Now we have three letters 14, 9 and 25. The product of the remaining two numbers is 12.
They can be of the form (1, 12), (2, 6) and (3, 4).
(1, 12) cannot be because it is given that the letter A is not a part of her name. 
(2, 6) cannot be because the alphabet B is already present in the husband’s name.
So the only possibility is (3, 4).
So the letters in her name are 14, 9, 25, 3 and 4 which are N, I, Y, C and D.
It is given that if the fourth letter from the left is shifted to second from the left then all the letters are in alphabetical order.
So her name must be “CINDY”.

Abhay, Basu, Chandu, Dinesh and Ehsan are given scores on the basis of three parameters strength, height and weight from 1 to 5. In strength category, score 5 denotes the strongest person and score 1 the weakest. Similarly, in height category, score 5 denotes the tallest and score 1 the shortest. In weight category, score 5 denotes the heaviest and score 1 denotes the lightest. The overall score of a person is the sum of all his scores in the three categories. No two person got same score in any category.
Further it is known that:
1. No one got the same score in all the three parameters.

2. The overall scores of no two person was same.

3. The person who got the highest overall score did not get highest score in any category.
4. Abhay who got the lowest overall score got 2nd highest score in the strength category.

5. The overall score of Basu, Ehsan ,Dinesh and Chandu is in descending order.
6. Abhay is the shortest person and Chandu is the heaviest person.
questions.question_text: Who ranks 3rd in the weight category?
questions.solution_text:
From (1), No person got same score in all the parameters.
From (2), The person who got the highest overall score did not get highest rank in any category.
Highest possible overall score = 3+4+4 = 11 (where 3,4,4 are scores in individual categories)
The lowest possible score = 1+1+2 = 4
All possible overall scores = 11,10,9,8,7,6,5,4
Since everyone gets different score from 1 to 5, the total sum of scores = 3(1+2+3+4+5) = 45
Only possible values of scores = 11,10,9,8,7
Now expressing them as sum of individual scores we get,
11 = 4+4+3
10=5+2+3, 5+1+4, 4+3+3, 4+2+2
9= 1+3+5, 2+2+5, 2+3+4
8=1+2+5, 1+3+4, 2+3+3, 2+2+4
7=1+2+4  (Since Abhay the lowest scorer will score 4 in the strength category and he got 1 in the height category from (6))
So his score can only be 7=1+2+4
Tabulating according to the conditions:
All the ranks are 11,10,9,8,7
So Abhay overall score is 7.
Overall score of Basu, Ehsan, Dinesh and Chandu is in descending order. Hence 
Overall score for Basu = 11, Ehsan=10, Dinesh=9 and Chandu=8
Now, since no two person has same rank in each category. Every score will appear three times.
Since there are only three 5s, score 8 = 1+2+5, score 9 = 1+3+5 or 2+2+5 and score 10 = 5+2+3 or 5+1+4
Since 11=4+4+3, 7=1+2+4, 4 has already appeared 3 times, 10=5+1+4 is rejected.
Also, 8=1+2+5 and 7=1+2+4, 2 has appeared 2 times, hence 9 = 2+2+5 is rejected.
Only possible case is 7=1+2+4, 8=1+2+5, 9=1+3+5, 10= 5+2+3, 11=4+4+3
Every score appears 3 times in this case.
Now score of Abhay in height will be 1 and score of Chandu in weight =5.
The complete table is: 
Ehsan has rank 3 in the weight category.

Read the following information carefully and answer the questions which follow.

Amit, Biswa, Chandan, Deepak and Gaurav participated in two different races. The first race was of 100 m and the second one of 200 m. Each one of them secured ranks among 1 to 5 in each of the races. Moreover, no two persons finished at the same position in 100 m race. The same is true for the 200 m race as well. Before the start of the first race, each one of them is assigned a seed among 1 to 5 based on their likelihood of winning. After each race, their seeds are revised based on the rank secured by them in the previous race. For example, the seeds for the second race will be the same as the ranks secured in the first race. Further, the following information is also known regarding each of the races.

100 m

1. Amit secured a better rank than Biswa in the 100 m race. The ranks of both of them were even numbers.

2. The difference between the ranks secured by Deepak and Gaurav in the 100m race is the same as the difference between the ranks secured by Gaurav and Chandan. Deepak finished the 100 m race before Gaurav and Chandan.

3. The sum of the absolute differences of the seeds of the 5 friends before and after the 100 m race is 8.

4. For only two pairs of friends, the absolute difference in the seeds before the first round and after the 100 m race is the same. However exactly one among the five friends had the highest absolute difference.

200 m

1. Biswa was not seeded 1 after the end of 200 m.

2. Sum of the absolute differences in the seeds of the five friends before 200 m and after 200 m is 10.

3. For exactly 3 friends,  the absolute differences of seeds before and after 200 m is 1.
questions.question_text: What can be the maximum value of the sum of the seeds of Deepak before 100 m, after 100 m and after 200 m?
questions.solution_text:
We can make a table showing the seeds at different stages.
Now we know that Amit secured a better rank than Biswa in 100 m and both of them have even numbered ranks. Hence, Amit must be second and Biswa must be 4th. From statement 2 about the 100 m race, we can determine the seeds of Deepak, Chandan and Gaurav at the end of 100 m race.
We know that the sum of the absolute differences for 5 friends is 8 and the two pairs of friends have the same absolute differences. Hence, the possible combinations are (0, 0, 2, 2, 4), (1, 1, 0, 3, 3), (0, 0, 3, 3, 2). However, (0, 0, 3, 3, 2) and (1, 1, 0, 3, 3) are not possible, since it has been mentioned that exactly one among the five friends had the maximum absolute difference. The only possible case is ( 0, 0, 2, 2, 4).

The chart below gives the data about the prediction made by three organisations, D-Voter, Poll Strat, and Today Chanakya, in recent election entry and exit polls. All three organisations predicted the vote share of three parties: DNA, INC and IPC.  After the election results, it is known that DNA got 55% of the votes, NIC received 40% of the votes, and IPC received 5% of the votes.

If the actual vote share of a party is equal or in between the entry and exit prediction of an organisation, that organisation is called Good Guesser for that party. There can be more than one good guesser for a party.

The prediction range of an organisation for a party is defined as the sum of the absolute difference between actual vote share and entry poll share and the absolute difference between actual vote share and exit poll share.

For, e.g., The prediction range for NIC by D-voter is |30-40|+|40-40| = 10.
questions.question_text: What is the sum of number of good guessers for all three parties?
questions.solution_text:
The actual vote share of DNA is 55%, NIC is 40% and IPC is 5%.
D-voter is Good guesser for DNA, NIC, IPC.
Poll strat is good guesser for IPC.
Today Chanakya is a good guesser for NIC, IPC.
So, the sum of number of good guessers for all three parties is 3+1+2 = 6.

There were a total of 8 distinct modes where a swimmer could participate.

There were a total of 300 swimmers and each of them participated in exactly one mode.

The additional instructions provided are :

1) The mean of the number of swimmers of regular and relay is equal to the difference between the number of regular and relay swimmers. There are more regular swimmers than relay swimmers.

2) The difference between the number of of swimmers in 200 m and 400 m is equal to the number of swimmers in 400 meters.

3) The sum of swimmers participating in 200 meter regular and 400 meter relay is 1.4 times the sum of swimmers in 400 meter regular and 200 meters relay.

4) The number of swimmers participating in Free style is 48 more than the total participants of 400 meter race.

5) The number of regular 400 meter swimmers is 16 less than the number of swimmers who take part in the 200 meter butterfly stroke.

Assuming all possible participants as variables and different possible participants and drawing a table for all the events :
In the question it was mentioned that total number of swimmers is 300. Hence o is 300.
Taking into the first condition we have the mean of regular and relay is equal to the difference between regular and relay.
Hence ((i+k)+(j+l))/2 = (i+k)-(j+l)
i+k = 3(j+l).
Since the total number of swimmers is 300 and (i+k) + (j+l) = 300.
i+k = 225, j+l = 75.
In condition 2 it was mentioned that the difference between the swimmers in 200 m and 400 m is equal to the number of swimmers participating in 400 meter swimming.
As per the variables this is given as m-n = n.
m =2*n.
m+n = 300.
m = 200, n = 100.
m = i+j = 200, n= k+l = 100.
Assuming i = x, k = 225-x since i+k = 225
Assuming j = y, l = 75-y since j+l = 75
In condition 3 it was mentioned that the sum of 200 meter regular swimmers and 400 meter relay swimmers is 1.4 times the 400 meter regular and 200 meter relay.
This in equation form is written by :
i+l = (7/5)(j+k).
5*i+5*l = 7*j+7*k.
5(x)+5(75-y) = 7(y)+7(225-x).
5*x+375-5*y = 7*y+1575- 7*x.
12*x- 12*y =1200.
x-y = 100.
i-j = 100.
I+j = 200.
i=150, j = 50.

e+f = 75

The meteorological department of City X recorded data on weather parameters over five days. Based on the data, the following chart is prepared which includes the maximum and minimum temperature recorded  in ($^{\circ\ }C$) and the humidity recorded in (%) on the five individual days.

We are given some addition information as follows: 

1. The wind speed (km/hr) recorded on the five days from Day 1 to Day 5 was 12, 15, 10, 8, and 14, respectively. 

2. The comfort level of a particular day is calculated using the comfort Index (CI) : $ \displaystyle \frac{\text{Max Temp} + \text{Min Temp}}{2} - \frac{\text{Humidity}}{4} $

3. Similarly, Wind Chill Factor (WCF) for a particular day is calculated using the formula: $ \displaystyle \text{Min Temp} - \frac{\text{Wind Speed}}{4} $
questions.question_text: Which day had the highest Comfort Index?
questions.solution_text:
From the chart above, we can note down the data into a table. 
Now, we need to find the comfort Index for each day. We know that the Comfort Index can be found using $ \displaystyle \frac{\text{Max Temp} + \text{Min Temp}}{2} - \frac{\text{Humidity}}{4} $ for the particular data of that day. 
CI of Day 1: $\dfrac{28+18}{2}-\dfrac{75}{4}=23-18.75=4.25$
CI of Day 2: $\dfrac{32+22}{2}-\dfrac{70}{4}=27-17.5=9.5$
CI of Day 3: $\dfrac{30+20}{2}-\dfrac{80}{4}=25-20=5$
CI of Day 4: $\dfrac{32+24}{2}-\dfrac{65}{4}=28-16.25=11.75$
CI of Day 5: $\dfrac{30+20}{2}-\dfrac{75}{4}=25-18.75=6.25$
So, clearly, we can say, Day 4 has the highest comfort index.

questions.passage_text: Ram participates in a game show wherein he is locked in a room. He has to open the door of the room to win the game. The door prompts the user to enter a 10 character password. The password contains 10 different characters. A computer counts the number of right characters and wrong characters entered after the third character is entered and then evaluates the same after each character is entered. If the total number of correct characters is less than a third of the total number of wrong characters, the game ends and Ram loses. If the person manages to enter 3 characters in their respective positions, the door opens. Also, if the person manages to key in 3 correct characters, say by the sixth character, the door opens (without having to enter the remaining 4 characters). If Ram wants to win the game on entering the sixth character to make it look less suspicious and if is known that all the six characters that Ram enters will be from the first six characters, then the number of possible passwords that Ram could enter is
questions.solution_text:
We know that the game has continued till Ram has entered the sixth character. Therefore, 2 out of the 5 characters entered before the sixth character must have been correct.
The number of ways in which 2 correct characters can be selected from 5 characters = 5C2 = 10 ways.
From these possibilities, we have to eliminate the case in which the 4th and 5th characters are correct (Since it would lead to the termination of the game).There is one such case. 
Therefore, the 2 correct characters can be selected in 10-1 = 9 ways. 
The remaining 3 characters can be deranged in 3! [ 1 - 1/1! + 1/2! - 1/3!] = 6/3 = 2 ways.
Therefore, the total number of passwords that Ram could use to win = 9*2 = 18.

Raghav have a cube with volume 729 $cm^3$, and which is painted with red colour on the outer surface area. He cuts the cube into 27 small cubes and coloured all the unpainted faces blue. 
Further the all the smaller cubes are cut to make cubes of 1 cm$^3$ and all the unpainted walls are painted black.
questions.question_text: How many cubes have all the walls painted black?
questions.solution_text:
The following diagram represents the process given in the question:
The large cube is of a dimension 9*9*9. This is cut into 27 medium cubes of dimension 3*3*3 and each of these medium cubes is cut into 27 cubes of dimension of 1*1*1. Hence 1 large cube => 27 medium cubes => 729 small cubes.
Of these small 729 cubes, we have to find those that are painted entirely black. The cube will be painted entirely black if it was not on the surface in either the large cube or the medium cube. Any cube that was on the surface in large cube would by default be on the surface in medium cube. So we have to find how many cubes are internal cubes in each medium cube. 
Number of internal cubes in a cube of side n = $(n-2)^3$ = $(3-2)^3$ = 1
Hence, each of the 27 medium cubes will have one cube which will not be painted red or blue. Thus, it will be entirely black. Thus, we have 27 entirely black cubes.

The lines x= 2015 and x= 2016 are parallel. Hence, opposite sides are parallel and the figure is a quadrilateral for any vegetable in between any two years.
Hence, the area would be found by the formula (height * average of parallel sides).

questions.question_text: Given that each potter makes exactly 30 pots in a month, the company realises that the profit from pot sales after hiring 30 workers monthly is twice that of hiring 20 workers. Find the selling price of 5 pots.
questions.solution_text:
We are told that each potter makes 30 pots a month. Since it is given that a month is a 30-day month, let us consider each worker makes 1 pot a day and calculate the cost per day to arrive at the profit comparisons. 
From the graph, we can see that the wage per worker when hiring 30 workers is 18 rupees a day, 
Bringing the total wage bill to 540 rupees a day. 
Since, there are only 17 wheels, the company will need to rent 13 more wheels, bring the rent to 26 rupees a day. 
Hence, the total expense per day when 30 workers are working will be 566 rupees a day. 
Consider the selling price of each pot as X. The total selling price every day will be 30X, 
And the profit, therefore, will be 30X-566
Similarly, the same calculations were run for 20 workers. We know the wage will be 20 rupees daily, bringing the total bill to 400 rupees. And the wheel rent cost will be an additional 6 rupees. Bringing the total cost to 406 rupees. 
The selling price from the pots each day will be 20X. 
And the profit, therefore, will be 20X-406
We are told that the profit when 30 workers are working is twice that when 20 workers are working. 
Drawing up the equation, we get, 
30X-566=2(20X-406)
30X-566=40X-812
10X=246
And since we are asked the selling price of 5 pots, 5X will be 123.

District Chenzen has three towns: A, B, and C. The following charts represent the percentage increase in the population, revenue, and number of shops in Chenzen over a 5-year span, with the second chart showing the contribution of towns A and B to the growth of the district over the given span of time. 

It is also known that for each year, each shop generates equal revenue, and every town member has an equal share in the number of shops in that town.
questions.question_text: What is the approximate percentage change in the average revenue generated by each shop from year 1 to year 5?
questions.solution_text:
Suppose the original number of shops was S and the original total revenue was R. 
This would give us the average revenue generated by the shops in year 1 as R/S
Over the span of five years the revenue changes to $\left(1.2\right)^2\left(1.3\right)\left(1.4\right)R$ while the number of shops change to $\left(1.1\right)^2\left(1.3\right)$S. 
Giving the average revenue to be $\frac{\left(1.2\right)^2\times\ 1.3\times\ 1.4}{1.1^2\times\ 1.3}\times\ \frac{R}{S}$
$\frac{1.44\times\ 1.4}{1.21}\times\ \frac{R}{S}=1.666\ \frac{R}{S}$
Hence the percentage change would be $\frac{\left(0.666\ \frac{R}{S}\right)}{\frac{R}{S}}\times\ 100=66.6\%$
The closest option is option B, 66%
Therefore, Option B is the correct answer.

Akshat and Akanksha were given some toffees and a bar of chocolate. They could divide the toffees among themselves equally, but each wanted the complete bar of chocolate for themselves. So they decided to play a game.
Akshat took 12 toffees and arranged them in two columns as shown.

The rules of the game are as follows:
1. Each person will get a turn alternately. During a turn, a person has to pick up at least 1 toffee. A person can pick up any number of toffees during their turn as long as they all belong to the same column.
For example, the first person to play can pick up 7 toffees, but not 8 as the eighth would belong to the other column.
2. The last person to pick up a toffee will win. He/She will be given the chocolate bar as well as half of the remaining toffees, which were not used in the game. The loser of the game will get the remaining half of the unused toffees. A person is allowed to keep the toffees he/she picked up during the game. 
Each person plays logically and to win.
questions.question_text: Akshat went first and picked up some toffees which ensured that he wins. What is the number of toffees that he picked up in the first turn?

In these types of games, one has to rely on backward induction. This means that we start from the end of the game and work towards the start.
Let (a,b) denote that there are 'a' and 'b' toffees in the two columns.
Since there is no constraint on how many toffees a person can pick up from a single column, the number of toffees left in a single column does not matter if the other column is empty. Hence to win, a player should never pick up all the toffees from a column. Since the players are playing logically and to win, they will never do this.
Hence on the second last turn, at least 1 toffee is left in each column.
If (1,1) toffees are left in each column, then the person whose turn it is next can pick up only one toffee and has to pick one up as per the rules. This leaves 1 toffee on the table, and the other person wins.
Hence if (1,1) toffees are left, the person whose turn it is next will lose.
But if a person wants to win, and leaves 1 toffee in one column and 2 or more toffees in the other, then the other player will just pick up one toffee from the column which has 2 toffees.

Initially, the number of toffees were (7,5). So Akshat will pick up 2 toffees to make it (5,5).

questions.passage_text:
ABC institute scheduled two seminars, one each on "Inflation 
Targeting" and "Women Empowerment in Informal Sector". The auditorium 
they had chosen for the seminar has sitting available for only 899 
people with that many chairs only arranged in the form of grid having 
dimensions $31\times29$. So the first 899 registered students are only allowed to attend the seminars. Each student was given a different registration number  from 1 to 899 at the time of registration. Also, it was mandatory for everyone to attend both the seminars and the same registration number is valid for both.

• Rows are numbered as row 1, row 2, row 3, ...... and row 31, and columns are numbered as column 1, column 2, column 3, ....., column 29.

• For "Inflation Targeting", students were asked to sit according to their registration number in row-wise manner. For example, student with registration number 1 sits on the seat in row 1 and column 1; student with registration number 2 sits on the seat in row 1 and column 2; and so on till registration number 29. Then student with registration number 30 sits on the seat in row 2 and column 1; student with registration number 31 sits on the seat in row 2 and column 2; and so on. And hence followed the same pattern till all the students got their seats.

• For "Women Empowerment in Informal Sector", students were asked to sit according to their registration number in column-wise manner. For example, student with registration number 1 sits on the seat in column 1 and row 1; student with registration number 2 sits on the seat in column 1 and row 2; and so on till registration number 31. Then student with registration number 32 sits on the seat in column 2 and row 1; the student with registration number 33 sits on the seat in column 2 and row 2; and so on. And hence followed the same pattern till all the students got their seats.
questions.question_text: How many students go on to seat on the same seat in both the seminars?
questions.solution_text:
Sitting arrangement of students during the seminar titled as “Inflation Targeting" is as given below, where number mentioned in any cell is the registration number of the student sitting on that seat.
If we observe the above table, we can see every row has consecutive numbers starting from 29×(row - 1) + 1.
So, the general term for the above table can be written as  $C_{ij}=29(i-1)+j,$ where $C_{ij}$ represents the seat in i th row and j th column.
Similarly, sitting arrangement of students during the seminar titled as “Women Empowerment in Informal Sector” is as given below
So, the general term for the above table can be written as $C_{ij}=31(j-1)+i$.
The student having same $C_{ij}$ value for both the seminars, got to sit on the same seat,
Therefore, $29\left(i-1\right)+j=31\left(j-1\right)+i$
or, $15j-14i=1$
Only possible positive integer solutions of the above equations are (1,1), (16,15) and (31,29).
Therefore, 3 students got to sit on same seat in both the seminars.

questions.solution_text:
From the line graph, we can make the following table mentioning the energy consumption by each sector in three months.

Now, we know the there is a subsidy policy that gives a 1% discount on the energy bill for every 1 GWh saved compared to the consumption in January. 
In February, the energy consumption was as follows for the Residential, Commercial, Industrial and Transportation sector as compared to January in the same order: (-10), (+5), (-10) and (-15)
So, the discount applicable for respective sectors on the February's energy bill = 10%, 0%, 10% and 15%
Similarly, in March, the energy consumption was as follows for the Residential, Commercial, Industrial and Transportation sector as compared to January in the same order: (-15), (-10), (-15) and (-5)
So, the discount applicable for respective sectors on the March's energy bill = 15%, 10%, 15% and 5%
So, in March, Transportation sector was offered subsidy worth 5% of Rs. 4,50,000 i.e. Rs. 22,500

questions.question_text: How many friends assigned rank 1 to Arsenal?

Each of the seven friends assigns rank 1, 2 and 3 to the teams. Hence, sum of the ranks assigned by a friend to all three teams = 1+2+3 = 6

Hence, using statement (3), we can say that the sum of the ranks assigned by all friends to Manchester United = x - 5. 
Similarly, by statement (4), we can say that the sum of the ranks assigned by all friends to Arsenal = x - 7.
$\Rightarrow$ $x+(x-5)+(x-7)=42$

Hence, we can say that there is just one unique case. Hence, we can figure out the breakup of ranks by individual friends to all three teams.

      Shipbuilding industry>Aviation industry>Automobile industry

Similarly , we can tabulate the price of the different grade of metals, we get

Aluminium Content, Aviation sector > shipbuilding industry > automobile industry

The only possible combination is

There is a box having nine cards with the numbers 1 to 9 written on them. Ravi picks up one card at a time, without being aware of the number and then places the numbers side by side to get a nine-digit code. Now, in the 9-digit code, if there is any number divisible by 2 immediately followed by a number divisible by 3, then this pair is called a rewarding pair. No two rewarding pairs can have a common number between them. Hence, if there are n rewarding pairs, there are 2n numbers among these pairs. At the end of the activity, Ravi is paid Rs 200 for each rewarding pair that the code has. If the code has 2 rewarding pairs, he is paid Rs 400, and so on. 

For example- The code 123456789 has two rewarding pairs -23- and -89-.

Based on the information, answer the questions that follow.
questions.question_text: If the final code is in the form of  __  2  __  __  __  6  __  __  9, how many codes are possible if Ravi wins Rs 600?
questions.solution_text:
Ravi gets three rewarding pairs. 
__  2  __  __  __  6  __  __  9
Now, only 'three' multiples of 3 are available, so we can have at most three rewarding pairs. Hence, all the multiples of 3 must come after a multiple of 2. Now, the number of multiples of 2 that are left is 3. Hence, the multiples of 2 come before a multiple of 3. 2 must be followed by 3. And 4 and 8 come before 6 and 9(in no particular order). Hence we get 2 cases.
__  2  3  __  4/8  6 __  4/8  9
Now, the remaining 3 spaces can be filled in 3! ways.
Hence a total of 2.3!, that is, twelve ways.

Also given, A and B left before D and F left immediately after B left => F also left before D.

In a game of card cricket, there are cards placed on a table, each card having an identifiable front(F) and a back(B) side. The first card has number 1 on F and 2 on B, the second card has number 3 on F and 4 on B, and so on..... The nth card has 2n-1 on F and 2n on B. These cards are shuffled, such that the F of each card is on the top and the B of each card is on the bottom. The batsman picks up any random card in each turn. If the number on either F or B of the card has a single digit, the batsman is termed OUT. Else if the number on either F or B has every digit as the same(ex: 555, 66, 1111), the batsman is termed OUT. If none of the above conditions is met, the batsman is awarded some runs in the following way:

S1 = Sum of digits of the number on F

S2 = Sum of digits of the number on B

R(Runs awarded to the batsman) = Maximum(S1, S2)

After every turn, the card is put back into the deck, so that it can be picked again.

Each time the batsman picks a card, it is termed as a delivery(similar to cricket). Runs scored in each delivery keeps on adding to the total score of the batsman. So, the total score of a batsman is the sum of the runs scored by him/her in all the deliveries faced. The batsman keeps picking up cards till he/she is termed OUT. After the batsman is out, the second player follows the same till he/she is termed out. The player with a higher total score wins the game. questions.passage_text: The distance between a school and a playground is 10 km. Three friends start travelling along a straight line from the school to playground such that two of them, A and B are travelling by cycle and the third, C starts walking. A drops B at a certain point along the way and goes back to pick up C. Meanwhile, B starts walking towards the playground as soon as A drops him. All three of them reach the playground at the same time. The speed of the cycle is 5 kmph and the walking speed of any of the three friends is 2kmph.
questions.question_text: What is the distance walked by C?
questions.solution_text:
Let the time for which A and B travelled by cycle be '$t_1$', time for which only A travelled by cycle be '$t_2$' and time for which A and C travelled by cycle be '$t_3$'.

B -> For time $t_1$, B travelled by cycle and for the remaining time B walked.

This implies, $5t_1+2\left(t_2+t_3\right)=10$ ...... (1)

A -> A cycled throughout the journey and covered more than 10 km.

$5t_1+5t_2+5t_3=10+2\left(5t_2\right)$

$5t_1-5t_2+5t_3=10$ ...... (2)

C -> For time $t_1+t_2$, C walked and for the remaining time A and C travelled by cycle.

This implies, $\left(t_1+t_2\right)2+5t_3=10$ ...... (3)

Equating (1) and (3), we get

$5t_1+2t_2+2t_3=2t_1+2t_2+5t_3$

$3t_1=3t_3$

$t_1=t_3$ ...... (4)

Equating (2) and (3), we get

$5t_1-5t_2+5t_3=2t_1+2t_2+5t_3$

$3t_1=7t_2$ ...... (5)

Solving (1), (4), and (5), we get

$5t_1+2t_2+2t_3=10$

$5t_3+2t_2+2t_3=10$

$7t_3+2\left(\frac{3t_3}{7}\right)=10$

$\frac{55t_3}{7}=10$

$\frac{11t_3}{7}=2$

$t_3=\frac{14}{11}$

$t_3=t_1=\frac{14}{11}$

From eqn (5), $3t_1=7t_2$

$3\left(\frac{14}{11}\right)=7t_2$

$t_2=\frac{6}{11}$

Distance walked by C = Time*speed = $2\left(t_1+t_2\right)=2\left(\frac{14}{11}+\frac{6}{11}\right)=\frac{40}{11}=3.63$km

The answer is option A.

The holder of the buck is Bina. The buck is passed immediately to the left, which means it is given to position 2 from 1, and it is received by Aarav. So, Aarav's position is 2.

The holder of the buck is Aarav. The buck is passed second to the right, which means it is given to the position 7 from 2, and the person receiving it is unknown.

The holder of the buck is unknown, but it is at position 7. The buck is passed immediately to the right, which means it is given to the position 6 from 7, and the person receiving it is Diya. Therefore, Diya's position is 6.

1) Passing the buck second to the right in round 4 and second to the right in round 5.
2) Passing the buck second to the left in round 4 and to the left in round 5.
3) Passing the buck to the left in round 4 and second to the left in round 5.

The value of F can only be 0 as F+F=F can only hold if F=0.

Also, A can only be 1(in the second column) because to get a carry of more than 1, B has to be a double-digit number which is not possible. (A carry is a digit that is transferred from one column of digits to another column of more significant digits.)

So the data can be tabulated as follows:

Since the last row in the third column is 0, the carry to the second column must have been 1, Hence B+1+1=11  => B=9

In the 4th column, H+H = 10 since a carry 1 has gone to the 3rd column. Hence H=5.

G+K must be 11 and the carry 1 goes to the next column, so C=1+1=2.

Now, G,K can take values (3,8), (4,7) and (5,6) in any order.

From 5th column G=J+1  => J=G-1

Case: G=3 and K=8, here J =2 which is not possible as C =2

Two players are playing a game called 'Pick an alpha'. In this game, there are 2 variables, the first one is 'a', the starting alphabet, and the second one 'n' the maximum range of alphabets starting from 'a'. The game proceeds as follows. One of the players picks an alphabet from the first n alphabets starting from 'a', say 'm', now the second player has to pick an alphabet from the first n alphabets starting from the alphabet just after 'm', and in a similar way, it continues till one player picks the alphabet Z. The player to choose Z loses the game. If at any point during the game, less than n alphabets remain, the player has to choose from these remaining alphabets. Both the players pick alphabets that maximise their chance to win.

Suppose, the value of 'a' is G and the value of n is 3. So, the first player has to pick an alphabet among G, H, I. Suppose he picks I. Then the second player has to pick among J, K and L. It continues in a similar fashion.

Based on the information given above, answer the questions that follow.
questions.question_text: If a = A and n = 5, what should the player starting the game choose initially so that he will definitely win the game?
questions.solution_text:
Let us think of it this way. The alphabets from A to Z can be thought of as numbers from 1 to 26 from which the two players pick.

If the player starting the game wants to win, he has to make sure that the other one is left with only one number, i.e the last number 26, in his last chance, which he has to pick necessarily.

Now let us consider a consecutive pair of chances. Whichever number a player picks from the n different choices, the second player can always pick a number such that to adjust it and make a sum of n + 1.

So, suppose, n = 6. If the first player chooses 3, the second player can choose 4 to make the sum 7.

So, 

The sum of all numbers should be the total number of characters, that is the alphabet representing 'a' to the alphabet 'Z'. In this case, 

26 - ( 3 x 7 + 1) = 4, i.e D.

In this question,

If a = A, this means a = 1.

n = 5.

n + 1 = 6

Total number of alphabets = 26

So, he should choose, 

26 - ( 6 x 4 + 1) = 26 - 25 = 1

Hence, A.

Alternate explanation:

Let the player who starts be P1 and the other be P2. We have to figure out which starting positions are definite losing positions.

Z is a losing position. If only Z is left, you have to pick Z and lose.

Y is a winning position as you will pick Y leaving opponent with Z which is a losing position. 

Any starting position from U to Y, you pick Y ensuring opponent loses.

Hence U-Y -> winning positions.

T is a losing position as no matter what you pick, opponent's starting position will fall in U-Y which are winning positions.

Similarly, O-S are winning positions as you should always choose S, putting opponent on T.

So we see the pattern that Z, T, N, H, B are losing positions. The corresponding numbers are 26, 20, 14, 8, 2. 

As B is definitely losing position, the first player should choose A to put the opponent on B.
